title: task edit-batch has the same active-tasks-only lookup restriction editOn had (QCLI-219)
description: TaskService.editBatch (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts, ~line 991) resolves each batch item's reference via workingTasks = [...initial.tasks] (active tasks/ location only) and a reference index built over that same set, so a batch item targeting a completed or archived record fails with task_not_found -- the identical bug QCLI-219 fixed for the single-item quest task edit path, in the batch path's own separate implementation. Not fixed as part of QCLI-219: editBatch uses an architecturally different locked-session write mechanism (beginTaskBatch/writeRecord/markApplied with journal recovery), not the plain repository.write()/writeLifecycle() split editOn uses, so the fix shape needs its own design rather than a direct port. Filed rather than silently left, per the fleet backlog campaign's rule that discovered-but-out-of-scope work gets its own task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Confirmed live whether editBatch actually reproduces task_not_found against a completed/archived reference (QCLI-219 confirmed this by source read only, not a live batch repro)

If confirmed: editBatch resolves batch items against the same cross-location set editOn now uses, and writes each retained-location item back to its own location rather than the active tasks/ directory -- verified against the locked-session/journal-recovery mechanics, not assumed compatible
Regression test covering a batch edit that includes at least one completed or archived item alongside an active one

plan: Widen editBatch's cross-location resolution: build workingTasks/workingLocations from taskRecords(initial) (all locations) instead of initial.tasks (active only), mirroring QCLI-219's editOn fix.

Extend TaskBatchSession.writeRecord(task, location?) so a session write can target completed/ or archive/tasks/ instead of always writeActiveRecord (tasks/); add LocalTaskRepository.writeRetiredRecord reusing the existing writeLifecycleRecord mkdir+temp+rename helper.
Fold retiredTasks (previously a separate read-only graph context) into the now-cross-location workingTasks so graph-touching batch edits validate over one consistent evolving set.

Add a live before/after regression test in test/cli-task-edit-batch.test.ts: a batch with an active + completed + archived item; confirm it fails with task_not_found pre-fix (verified by stashing the source change) and succeeds post-fix, writing each retained item back to its own location with no stray tasks/ duplicate.
implementationNotes: Confirmed live (AC1): stashed the source fix (src/application/tasks/{tasks,local-task-repository}.ts) with the new regression test in place, ran it against unmodified editBatch -- applied=1, failed=2 (the two retired-location items both hit task_not_found), matching QCLI-219's already-diagnosed shape exactly. Restored the fix; same test then applied=3, failed=0. Fixed (AC2): workingTasks/workingLocations in editBatch now derive from taskRecords(initial) (all locations), not initial.tasks (active only); TaskBatchSession.writeRecord gained an optional location param (default "tasks") that routes to the existing writeActiveRecord for "tasks" and to a new writeRetiredRecord (reusing the private writeLifecycleRecord mkdir+temp+rename helper) otherwise -- verified against the locked-session mechanics specifically: the batch session's lock file is the same .quest/tasks/.write.lock writeLifecycle acquires, so writing a retired location's path directly for the duration of an already-open session is safe, not a new concurrency surface. Regression test (AC3) added in test/cli-task-edit-batch.test.ts: one batch with an active + completed + archived item, verified fails before the fix and passes after (see AC1), and asserts no stray duplicate lands in .quest/tasks/ for the retired items. bun run check: 428/428 tests green, typecheck/lint/format/layer-check clean.
finalSummary: editBatch had the identical active-tasks-only lookup restriction editOn had before QCLI-219 fixed it: a batch item referencing a completed or archived record failed with task_not_found, and even when reference resolution was later widened its write path (session.writeRecord -> writeActiveRecord) was hardcoded to .quest/tasks/, which would have written a stray duplicate there. Fixed by building the batch's working set from taskRecords(initial) (all locations) instead of initial.tasks, and adding a location-aware write (TaskBatchSession.writeRecord(task, location?) -> LocalTaskRepository.writeRetiredRecord for completed/archived items, reusing the existing writeLifecycleRecord mkdir+temp+rename helper). The batch's own lock file is the same .quest/tasks/.write.lock writeLifecycle acquires, so this is safe within an open session. Verified live, not just by source read: the new regression test in test/cli-task-edit-batch.test.ts reproduces task_not_found against a completed and an archived item before the fix (confirmed by temporarily stashing the source change) and passes after, asserting no stray duplicate lands in tasks/. bun run check: 428/428 tests green.
